observation: The initial self-shape implementation encoded the complete governed lifecycle directly in GitHub Actions and repeated the changed-file list for plan and report. That made CI the owner of process logic and created another place where the lifecycle could drift. The lifecycle was extracted to a compact repository-owned shell runner and CI became wiring only.

evidence.summary: The repository-owned tools/self-shape-dogfood.sh derived 29 changed files from the real merge-base, drove PLAN through CLOSE, and finished with review status ok, no drift, and a complete manifest. PHP 8.3, 8.4, 8.5 and the installed release-set dogfood were all green in the same run.

hypothesis: CI should invoke a repository-owned dogfood runner rather than define the governed lifecycle itself; deriving scope from Git should also remove duplicated file lists without changing behavior.
validated_conclusion: GitHub Actions is the executor, not the owner, of the self-shaping lifecycle. Keep that lifecycle in tools/self-shape-dogfood.sh and derive the PR file scope from Git so PLAN and REPORT share one source of truth and can run locally as well as in CI.
